name: Free Choices in a Certified Tree Lift Can Create Directed Cycles
statement: The representation-map lifting construction over a tree reduction does not preserve acyclicity for every allowed choice. A 12-vertex expansion over a four-vertex path has a certified lifted representation map containing a directed six-cycle; changing one free vertical-source bit yields an acyclic representation map, and the same expansion has an explicit corner peeling. Thus the example refutes arbitrary-choice preservation, while retaining existence of an acyclic choice.
proof: The displayed out-map satisfies nonclashing, outgoing-cube, and unique-sink conditions, but direct evaluation on its six listed vertices gives a directed cycle. Flipping the sole free bit reverses only one vertical assignment; the upper path and lower cube are then separately acyclic and every vertical edge points downward. The independent twelve-vertex deletion order verifies ordinary corner peelability.
